Standard AI generation produces scripts that feel like audio Wikipedia summaries or dry college essays. Even when surface-level clichés (em dashes, rule-of-three, promotional fluff) are removed using tools like `/humanizer`, the underlying script will still suffer from **structural sterility**:
- **Symmetric Weighting:** Giving every topic equal length (e.g. exactly 60 seconds per item) with no editorial hierarchy.
- **Academic Citation Dead-Weight:** Introducing sources as bibliographies (*"According to a 2018 study by Dr. Smith..."*) rather than cinematic scenes.
- **Linear / Monotone Emotion:** Maintaining a constant, polite educational hum rather than weaponizing tonal contrast and dark humor.
- **Delayed Immersion:** Wasting 15–45 seconds clearing the throat (*"In this video, we're going to dive into..."*).

High-retention faceless documentary channels (averaging 3.5M–6.3M views per hit video and RPMs between $40–$65) follow an invariant structural law:

$$\mathbf{\text{Retention Score}} = \frac{\text{Tactile Sensory Specificity} \times \text{Tonal Whiplash} \times \text{Named Source Density}}{\text{Time-to-Topic Latency} \times \text{Abstract Cognitive Friction}}$$

## 2. Dimension 1: Hook Engineering & Cold Open Formulas (0:00–0:30)

Every millisecond before the viewer is hooked represents audience drop-off. The first 30 seconds must accomplish three tasks: (1) Introduce the primary topic subject within **0.00 to 1.50 seconds**, (2) Deliver an unambiguous **Curiosity Gap or Moral Threat** by 0:15, and (3) Lock in the **Macro Promise** of the video by 0:30.
